title: POC scoping - Data handling & retention - Horizon Medical
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling: PII, redaction, retention, prompt storage, and logging during a 6-week POC. Agreed success criteria, workload sizing for 10k daily requests, and next steps to share SOC2/KMS docs and set benchmark window.
next_steps: Redwood: send SOC2 + security whitepaper and KMS integration doc (by 2026-09-28)
Customer: share sample prompt patterns and sanitized dataset for benchmark (by 2026-10-01)
Schedule technical benchmark run and seeding window (target week of 2026-10-12)
Follow-up call to review benchmark results and SLA options (w/ procurement)
action_items: Owner: Emma Chen; Item: Send SOC2 + KMS + data handling playbook; Due: 2026-09-28
Owner: Maya Singh; Item: Provide representative prompt samples and 48-hour anonymized logs; Due: 2026-10-01
Owner: Ravi Patel; Item: Draft benchmark plan (latency, p50/p95, token cost), include dedicated vs hosted configs; Due: 2026-10-05
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Emma Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lisa Moreno (Horizon Head of AI), Tom Briggs (Horizon Security), Maya Singh (PM)

Summary: quick scoping focused on how Horizon wants PII handled in the POC, what we log, retention windows, and the benchmark sizing. Agreed on ~6 week POC with an initial 1-week benchmark run.

00:00:00 Emma Chen: hey everybody, thanks for jumping on, uh we'll kick off, I'm Emma from Redwood, with Ravi our SE, why don't we do quick intros then jump into goals for the POC
00:00:14 Lisa Moreno: hi yeah Lisa here, Head of AI at Horizon, we want to validate LLM assistant for triage and routing, main risk is PHI/PII leakage, also curious abt latency and cost
00:00:28 Tom Briggs: Tom, security architect, focusing on logging, encryption, and retention; we can't keep prompts longer than X days without controls
00:00:35 Ravi Patel: thanks, quick note, we will cover hosted vs dedicated for the POC, and how logs and prompt storage behave in each
00:01:05 Maya Singh: PM, owning timeline, target is a 6 week POC and then procurement if results meet thresholds
00:01:22 Emma Chen: perfect, main agenda: define success criteria, workload sizing for bench, data handling rules (what's redacted, retention), and next steps

00:03:10 Ravi Patel: for workload sizing you mentioned about 10k requests/day in peak — is that correct? and what's average tokens per request?
00:03:22 Lisa Moreno: correct on peak, average prompt ~120 tokens, responses ~300 tokens, we have bursts during morning rounding so p95 matters more than average
00:03:39 Ravi Patel: great, so for benchmarking we'll target p50/p95 latency, token cost, and throughput. We'll run an initial warmup on hosted endpoints and then compare with a dedicated pool if you need lower p95

00:05:02 Tom Briggs: on data handling, our strict requirement: PHI can't be stored in plaintext in logs or persistent prompt storage. We need to see how Redwood handles prompt retention, whether prompts are stored by default, and if we can disable that or redact PII automatically
00:05:21 Emma Chen: yes, good question. By default Redwood's hosted API keeps logs for troubleshooting but we have retention controls and redaction pipelines. For POC we can set retention to 7 days and enable PII redaction — we also have a private deployment option if you require zero-persist host storage
00:05:43 Tom Briggs: when you say redaction pipeline, is that pre-send or post-receive? we need to know if anything ever lands unredacted in logs.
00:05:55 Ravi Patel: it's both: we offer client-side masking pattern guidance (regex templates) and server-side redaction flows. For hosted, raw request bodies are encrypted at rest, and we run automated redaction before storing in long-term logs. There are edge cases though, e.g., free-text in attachments — those need policy rules
00:06:20 Lisa Moreno: okay can you confirm KMS integration? must be able to manage keys per customer
00:06:28 Emma Chen: yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) for Private deployments and for Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key options; hosted can use customer-managed keys in certain enterprise plans

00:08:00 Maya Singh: timeline question — we proposed 6 weeks, what's realistic to get benchmark data and security review done?
00:08:12 Ravi Patel: recommended split: week 0 provisioning & config, week 1 benchmark window (3-5 days of ramped traffic), weeks 2-5 POC evaluation and feature validation, week 6 wrap + procurement handoff. If you supply sanitized prompts quickly we can accelerate the benchmark

00:09:30 Tom Briggs: what about prompt storage concerns — do you store prompts in backups or snapshots? retention is important for compliance and we have to show data flow for audits
00:09:44 Emma Chen: prompts are stored according to retention settings; snapshots/backups are also subject to retention and our backup lifecycle. For POC we recommend setting snapshot retention to match POC window (eg 14 days) and we can provide an export of stored prompts and a deletion confirmation at end of POC
00:10:10 Lisa Moreno: deletion confirmation is critical, also need an audit trail of who accessed logs and when
00:10:18 Ravi Patel: audit logs are available — we capture token-level access metadata and who/what client called the endpoint. We can produce an access audit for the benchmark window

00:12:05 Tom Briggs: on redaction accuracy: do you perform entity detection for PII? e.g., detect MRNs, SSNs, phone numbers in free text?
00:12:16 Ravi Patel: we have built-in PII detectors that run prior to storage, they use regex + ML models, accuracy isn't perfect so we recommend customer-specific regex rules for medical identifiers. For highly sensitive fields we can configure to drop or hash those tokens before they touch any long-term store
00:13:00 Lisa Moreno: can we get a list of what Redwood logs by default vs what can be turned off? we need to present to legal
00:13:12 Emma Chen: yes will share a table: default logs (timestamps, anonymized metadata, request id, partial prompts) and optional logs (full prompt, model outputs) which can be disabled. For POC we recommend disabling full prompt logging and enabling only anonymized payloads

00:15:30 Ravi Patel: on benchmarks — p95 latency target you want under what number? you mentioned user-facing triage, so under 800ms p95 is ideal?
00:15:42 Lisa Moreno: yes under 800ms ideally, if not we need backlog-friendly UX. p50 should be under 250ms for snappy feel
00:15:55 Ravi Patel: good, we'll capture p50/p95 and token costs in the benchmark, and compare hosted v dedicated; dedicated typically gives better p95 but costs more

00:18:00 Maya Singh: success criteria — what are we measuring to call the POC a win?
00:18:11 Lisa Moreno: success is: 1) p95 < 800ms on production-weighted workload, 2) no PII persisted beyond 7 days unless expressly stored, 3) redaction false negative rate < 0.1% on a validated sample, 4) cost per 1k requests within agreed threshold
00:18:30 Emma Chen: captured — we'll include these in the POC plan and instrument checks against them

00:20:05 Tom Briggs: on legal/procurement: we will need subprocessor list, SOC2 type II, DPA, and the ability to redact individual records on demand
00:20:18 Emma Chen: we have SOC2, DPA, and can provide subprocessors. For record-level deletion we offer APIs and can provide deletion proofs at the end of retention window

00:22:40 Ravi Patel: for the benchmark plan I propose: 3 day warmup with ramp to 10k/day, collect p50/p95, tail latencies, token throughput; run test on your representative prompt set; config matrix: hosted default, hosted with PII-redaction enabled, dedicated medium instance, and private demo if you want to test KMS flow
00:23:02 Lisa Moreno: can we run a dark test with real-ish data behind VPN? we can't send PHI to hosted env without further controls
00:23:15 Emma Chen: yes we can do on-prem or VPC-private demo. For hosted we can offer a sanitized dataset test first, and we can run a VPC-connected dedicated test for realistic traffic behind your network controls

00:25:50 Tom Briggs: logging for troubleshooting — we sometimes need full request dumps for debugging. How do you support that without violating retention?
00:26:00 Ravi Patel: we support ephemeral diagnostic logs with elevated access that are time-bounded and require approval; they can be kept for narrow windows and then purged; all access is audited. We recommend using ephemeral debug mode during the benchmark and then revert to anonymized logs

00:28:30 Maya Singh: cost concern — we need a rough estimate for the POC to include in budget, especially comparing hosted vs dedicated for 10k/day with token sizes you mentioned
00:28:45 Emma Chen: we'll send a POC pricing sheet; rough back-of-envelope: hosted POC estimated $X/day (we'll provide actual numbers in the sheet) and dedicated has a monthly committed cost but gives better p95; we'll include token cost breakdown and expected infra variance

00:30:10 Lisa Moreno: around prompt storage — are prompts used to retrain or for model improvement? data residency rules matter there
00:30:22 Emma Chen: by default we do not use customer prompts to improve public models; it's opt-in for model improvement and fully documented. For Horizon's PII constraints we'll keep all prompts isolated and not use them for training; we can include that in the DPA
00:31:00 Tom Briggs: one more technical: what about KV cache dumps and intermediate states — anything persisted that could include user tokens?
00:31:12 Ravi Patel: KV cache is ephemeral and resident on the serving node; we don't persist raw KV cache across requests except for session continuation when you opt-in. For the POC we can disable session persistence so KV remains ephemeral in memory only

00:33:40 Maya Singh: reminders on timeline: we'll share sanitized prompts by 10/01, Redwood to send security docs by 9/28, benchmark plan by 10/05, and target benchmark week of 10/12

00:35:10 Emma Chen: yep, and we'll set retention to 7 days for POC logs, disable full prompt logging by default, enable server-side PII redaction. We'll provide an audit export at the end of the benchmark window

00:37:00 Lisa Moreno: for redaction we will also send a small annotated dataset to measure false negative rate, is that okay?
00:37:12 Ravi Patel: absolutely, that helps tune the regex rules and ML detector thresholds; we'll iterate on that during weeks 2-3

00:39:20 Tom Briggs: legal will want to confirm subprocessor list and how deletion API behaves; could we get an example deletion request/response?
00:39:33 Emma Chen: yes we'll include API spec examples and a deletion proof artifact format in the security packet

00:41:55 Maya Singh: any blockers from Redwood side to start once we sign the POC SOW?
00:42:06 Emma Chen: none, just need your sanitized sample dataset and signature on SOW; we'll provision dedicated pool if requested and set up KMS access if you choose that path

00:44:40 Ravi Patel: technical note: for the p95 targets we'll likely recommend dedicated or specialized instance type for low tail latency; we can show typical p95 numbers from similar health customers in the benchmark plan
00:45:00 Lisa Moreno: makes sense — also need a short memo for compliance explaining how prompts are handled during the POC
00:45:10 Emma Chen: we'll include a one-page data flow diagram and memo in the packet

00:47:20 Tom Briggs: okay seems we have alignment on controls. minor thing: please confirm data residency for backups — we need backups in us-east only
00:47:32 Emma Chen: noted, we'll set backup region to us-east for the POC and include that in config

00:49:55 Maya Singh: final recap and next steps?
00:50:05 Emma Chen: recap: 6-week POC, bench week of 10/12, Redwood to provide SOC2/KMS/docs by 9/28, Horizon to provide sanitized prompts by 10/01, POC pricing and benchmark plan by 10/05, follow-up call to review results after benchmark. action items recorded
00:50:28 Lisa Moreno: thanks all, really appreciate how specific you're being on retention and redaction
00:50:36 Tom Briggs: thanks, looking forward to the security packet
00:50:40 Emma Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the packet and SOW draft
00:51:00 Meeting end
notes: Agreed retention 7 days for POC logs (can be adjusted)
Disable full prompt logging by default for POC
Benchmark matrix to include hosted/default, hosted+redaction, dedicated, and VPC/dedicated with KMS
